sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Retailing of Smart IoT Devices and Home Automation

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Double Taxation Agreement with the United States (in force, as amended)
Double Taxation Agreement with the People's Republic of China (in force)
Double Taxation Agreement with the United Kingdom (in force)
EU Treaty framework (TFEU), ICSID Convention and EU Anti-Tax-Avoidance Directives

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended by the Law of 25 March 2020; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 February 2018 on UBO filing; CSSF Regulation 12-02 as amended; CSSF Circular 18/698; Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended, incorporating the SCSp under the Law of 23 July 2016.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (official register accessible to competent authorities and persons with legitimate interest; public disclosure restricted per CJEU jurisprudence)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized or authenticated copy of the SCSp partnership agreement (contrat de société) or draft for deposit
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of Luxembourg or competent notary in the origin state of the partners

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing and non-insolvency for each corporate or individual beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: RCS Luxembourg for local entities; competent company registry or court in the foreign origin jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney empowering the Luxembourg domiciliary agent to execute pre-incorporation filings and UBO declarations
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign partner or beneficial owner's notary, consulate, or competent local authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copies of passports and address proof for all individuals identified as beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing state's passport authority, police authority, or notary

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against OFAC/SDN, UN Security Council consolidated lists, EU restrictive measures, and domestic Luxembourgian lists; mandatory PEP identification of all beneficial owners and senior management per CSSF Regulation 12-02 and Circular 18/698; risk-based enhanced due diligence applied to source-of-wealth and source-of-funds for any PEP or elevated-risk nexus.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) electronic portal at https://www.lbr.lu serving the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be rendered in the Latin alphabet; French, German, Luxembourgish, or other modern European languages are acceptable; non-Latin scripts require an official Roman-script transliteration. The name must not be misleading, contrary to public order, or identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name. An SCSp must clearly include 'SCSp' or 'Société en commandite spéciale' in its corporate designation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant must file a written administrative appeal with the Director of the RCS within one month of the refusal decision, stating the legal basis and proposed revised name; any further recourse lies to the Administrative Court (Tribunal administratif) within three months of the rejection decision, per the Luxembourg law of 21 June 1999 on administrative procedure.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible in principle for a low-risk IoT retail business; the SCSp must maintain a registered office address in Luxembourg and retain a local corporate services provider. A pure virtual office without any administrative presence may attract enhanced AML scrutiny and is accepted only where statutory records are physically accessible in Luxembourg.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 8% annualized likelihood of an unannounced physical on-site inspection under CSSF risk-based AML supervision for this low-risk standard retail profile.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation legal consultation and UBO/AML compliance review by a senior Luxembourg corporate attorney
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg law firm regulated by the Luxembourg Bar
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per hour (EUR 350-450 per hour)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed of the SCSp partnership agreement (voluntary but recommended for banking and cross-border acceptance)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public of Luxembourg (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff under Luxembourg notarial fee regulations

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance, RCS registration, and publication fees
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés via Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official RCS/LBR registration and publication tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO declaration processing and filing fee
AML/KYC due diligence pack covering PEP, OFAC, UN, EU sanctions screening and CDD on all beneficial owners
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Accredited Luxembourg AML compliance provider and fiduciary

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization processing plus certified translations
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent authorities of the origin jurisdiction and Luxembourg certified translators
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official apostille tariffs plus prevailing certified translation market rate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and corporate services allocated to the pre-incorporation phase
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg corporate services provider / domiciliation agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per annum, pro-rated to pre-incorporation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Ministerial sensitive-token approval buffer (not required for ISIC 4791 retail IoT hardware; shown at zero)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministère de la Justice du Luxembourg
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Not applicable; statutory fee would apply only if a sensitive-token name waiver were sought

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, in particular Articles 103-1 et seq. for the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp); Law of 19 December 2002 concerning the register of commerce and companies and the accounting and annual accounts of undertakings.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) trading as the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg City
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Partnership deed (acte de société/contrat de société) filed with the RCS, together with the RCS registration declaration, and publication in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for an SCSp; the partnership agreement freely fixes the amount and form of partners’ contributions, and no escrow account, capital blockage or notarial deposit certificate is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that each partner's capital subscription and contribution commitments to the Société en Commandite Spéciale are approved and credited as set out in the partnership deed; RESOLVED, that the SCSp's registered office be established at [specific Luxembourg address], with the Luxembourg Business Registers authorised to file the deed and publish the incorporation; RESOLVED, that [Name] be appointed manager (gérant) for the duration of the SCSp, with full power to represent the SCSp, open bank accounts, appoint service providers, sign commercial contracts, and make compliance filings; RESOLVED, that the manager is authorised to obtain insurance, perform regulatory filings, and complete all remaining formation formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary and/or the partners; notarial form is required only where an immovable contribution is made
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the deed containing the SCSp's legal name, registered office in Luxembourg, corporate object, identity and contributions of partners, duration, management powers of the gérant, profit-sharing rules and liquidation procedure. Execute the deed in private writing or notarial form as applicable; have each partner and the accepting manager sign the instrument.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID of each general and limited partner
Proof of residential address of each partner
Certificate of name availability or RCS name search result
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry or notary raises a formal objection, correct and re-execute the deed; where an article is declared contrary to mandatory law, file a rectification deed or amend the partnership agreement and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Registration with Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) electronic filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed partnership deed together with the RCS registration declaration through the LBR online portal. Pay the applicable RCS filing fee and provide certified translations where the deed language is not French, German or Luxembourgish. The RCS assigns the registration number and automatically forwards the filing for publication.
required_dossiers: Statement of the gérant accepting office
Identity documents of partners and manager
Registered office consent letter or lease agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to any RCS query within eight days by submitting the missing document, corrected translation or notarised attestation; a re-filing fee may apply, after which registration proceeds.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Publication in the Electronic Compendium (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – RESA publication office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following registration, the RCS publishes the partnership particulars in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations. The SCSp should obtain the RESA extract and retain it as conclusive evidence of legal existence for banking, leasing and counterparty due-diligence purposes.
required_dossiers: Copy of partnership deed as registered
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the published particulars contain an error, request rectification of the RESA publication pursuant to the Law of 10 August 1915 and submit a corrective declaration to the RCS.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for Tax, VAT and National Identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) and the Luxembourg registration authority for tax numbers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, register the SCSp with the AEDT for income tax, subscription tax and VAT purposes. Request a Luxembourg VAT identification number and, where applicable, a national business number; complete the VAT registration prior to the first taxable transaction, specifying the expected turnover from retail sales of smart home IoT hardware.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of partners and manager
Description of activities and projected turnover
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax file is suspended or queried, submit a written response with certified translations and the requested turnover disclosures; if a VAT number is already issued, no re-registration is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register as Employer with Social Security and for Occupational Accident Cover
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the SCSp intends to employ staff, complete the employer registration with CCSS within eight days of the first engagement and register each employee for sickness, pension and accident insurance. If the SCSp begins with no employees, this step is optional but may be completed voluntarily to expedite future hiring.
required_dossiers: Copy of gérant and partners' identification documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late employer registration is subject to administrative penalties; file a late-declaration cure with a letter explaining the delay and request a penalty adjustment or payment plan from CCSS.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Municipal Premises, Fire Safety and Occupational Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Competent municipal administration (Administration communale) and the Occupational Health and Safety Inspectorate (ITM)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the classified establishment declaration or the municipal occupancy dossier for the retail, office and storage premises. Obtain the fire safety clearance, structural conformity certificate and occupational safety review before the premises are used for commercial activity.
required_dossiers: Fire safety certificate or inspection report
Occupational health and safety inspection certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality refuses or suspends the operation, remedy by installing fire detection and extinguishing equipment, reducing storage quantities below threshold limits, or applying for a derogation; re-inspection then lifts the suspension.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Luxembourg Ministry of the Economy (Ministère de l'Économie) and the competent municipal administration for classified establishments and physical occupation of commercial premises
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Classified establishment declaration (déclaration d'établissement classé) or municipal occupancy and fire-safety clearance for retail warehousing and distribution of IoT devices

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration / simple declaration under the Classified Establishments regime; no full EIA Report required for dry storage and online retailing of smart home IoT hardware absent hazardous-waste thresholds
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater discharge permits required for non-manufacturing retail; maintain compliance with EU RoHS and WEEE take-back obligations for electrical and electronic equipment; register packaging waste and comply with national packaging recovery quotas; keep indoor VOC levels within occupational threshold limit values; boundary noise limits generally not to exceed 40 dB(A) during night-time in mixed-use zones

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the municipal fire authorities or Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours; structural load inspection for storage racks and mezzanine floors; workplace clearance from the Luxembourg Occupational Health Inspectorate (ITM) covering emergency exits, electrical conformity, and suitable lighting and ventilation for retailwarehouse operations

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) — Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) — Luxembourg Registration, Estates and VAT Administration; consolidated single-access portal: MyGuichet.lu (https://guichet.public.lu).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The SCSp is fiscally transparent, so the partnership itself is not ordinarily the direct taxpayer. Registration sequence: (1) enroll the SCSp with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) through MyGuichet.lu to obtain the RCS registration number and the statutory matricule (national business identification number). (2) Apply for a Luxembourg VAT number with the AEDT using the electronic VAT registration form (form 010C) where the SCSp makes taxable supplies and does not benefit from the EUR 35,000 small-business exemption; a non-resident partner acting through the SCSp must also appoint a Luxembourg tax agent or VAT representative (représentant responsable) when the SCSp has no fixed establishment in Luxembourg. (3) Register each non-resident partner for direct tax purposes with the ACD via the non-resident registration procedure (e-form 160A) to obtain Luxembourg income tax reference numbers. Supporting documents include the notarized partnership deed, RCS excerpt, proof of registered office, identity documents of general partner(s) and ultimate beneficial owners, and a completed AML/KYC pack for the depositary or bank. The AEDT routinely issues the VAT number within 15 business days of a complete filing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box regime exists in Luxembourg. The SCSp is default-transparent for Luxembourg corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax; income, gains, and net wealth are attributed pro rata to partners. If all partners are collective entities fully liable to Luxembourg corporate income tax, the partners may jointly elect to treat the SCSp as opaque and subject it to entity-level taxation; that election is binding and irreversible for the life of the partnership. EU anti-hybrid rules (implemented by the Luxembourg Law of 21 December 2018) may neutralize mismatches where the SCSp is treated as transparent in Luxembourg and opaque in the partner jurisdiction; no specific hybrid-mismatch re-election mechanism exists beyond reliance on the general anti-abuse rule and ATAD 1/2 carve-outs.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 (annual turnover below which the small-business exemption under Article 57 of the Luxembourg VAT Law may apply); EUR 10,000 (EU-wide cross-border distance-sales and OMP threshold above which Luxembourg VAT applies to B2C sales of IoT hardware by an EU-established retailer); no registration threshold for a Luxembourg-established taxable person holding an RCS commercial registration or for supplies of goods subject to excise rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory B2G e-invoicing via PEPPOL (BIS 3.0) in force since 1 January 2020 for all invoices issued to Luxembourg public-sector buyers. Mandatory domestic B2B structured e-invoicing (EN 16931/PEPPOL) was enacted by the Luxembourg law of 18 July 2024 and applies in phases from 1 January 2026 (large taxpayers) and generally from 1 January 2027 (all taxable persons). No real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control (CTC) engine, or digital stamping platform operates at present; periodic VAT returns, VIES recapitulative statements, and Intrastat declarations are filed electronically via MyGuichet.lu or the AEDT e-filing portal, and the new e-invoicing regime introduces structured audit-file (SAF-T) extraction expectations in line with the future e-reporting framework.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating at 0% Luxembourg VAT applies to: (i) export supplies of goods physically leaving the EU customs territory, provided transport begins no later than 90 days after the supply and the goods leave the EU within that period; (ii) intra-Community supplies of goods to a counterparty holding a valid VAT registration number confirmed on VIES; (iii) supplies of services directly linked to exported goods or to offshore goods for processing, where the recipient is established outside the EU and the place-of-supply rules put the supply outside Luxembourg. The SCSp retailing smart-home IoT hardware may claim zero rating for direct exports to non-EU customers, but distance sales of EU-stored goods to EU consumers are taxed at destination through the Union OMP scheme or local registration once the EUR 10,000 threshold is exceeded.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (EX-A / DAU) lodged electronically through Luxembourg Customs or the ICS system, showing the SCSp as exporter
Bill of Lading, CMR consignment note, or Air Waybill evidencing physical exit of the goods from the EU customs territory
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank documentation proving receipt of export payment in foreign currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg VAT law and Customs law impose rigorous scrutiny of export substantiation. If zero-rating is claimed without satisfactory customs exit proof, the AEDT retrospectively claws back VAT at the standard 17% rate with statutory late-payment interest of 0.6% per month. Administrative fines reach EUR 4,000 per violation for invoicing or registration breaches; intentional fraud triggers fines of up to EUR 25,000 or one to three times the evaded tax, plus imprisonment under the Luxembourg criminal code for forgery of customs declarations, transport documents, or export evidence. The standard limitation period for assessment is 5 years, extended to 10 years in cases of fraud or bad faith. Documentary retention of the full export bundle for at least 10 years is recommended given the extended fraud look-back window and OMP compliance risks.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) in conjunction with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for payment and FX licensing supervision, and the Ministry of Finance for balance-of-payments statistical reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a fully euroised EU member state with unrestricted current and capital account convertibility. There is no FX control authority and no exchange licensing regime for capital injections, trade settlements, profit distributions or liquidation proceeds. The SCSp is fiscally transparent, so distributions to partners are generally outside Luxembourg withholding tax and may be remitted freely in EUR or any convertible currency, subject only to global EU sanctions, AML/KYC checks and statistical reporting. Profits and capital may be converted without prior central bank approval.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg does not impose export proceeds surrender requirements or mandatory conversion ratios. Export receipts may be retained in EUR or foreign currency without restriction. However, cross-border payments above the BCL de minimis statistical reporting threshold (EUR 12,500) must be declared by the reporting bank to the BCL under the ECB balance-of-payments and international investment position framework.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account / Multi-currency Treasury Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium. A Luxembourg-authorised EMI or payment institution operating under PSD2 and CSSF Circular 18/698 may be used as a high-speed collection rail for e-commerce sales from Stripe and Shopify Payments, but it may not engage in credit-taking, investment services, or unrestricted treasury management. Offshore digital EMIs without an EEA passport are not viable for Luxembourg cross-border clearing because they cannot lawfully provide payment services in the EEA and would not be accepted by tier-1 banks as underlying treasury rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally required for ultimate beneficial owners and authorised signatories during initial onboarding of a Luxembourg SCSp. Remote opening may be available in narrow cases under CSSF Circular 19/722 and the Act of 12 November 2004 on AML/CFT using a qualified electronic signature and video identification, but in practice most tier-1 banks mandate an in-person interview at the Luxembourg branch before opening a capital escrow or operational account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated SCSp with multiple international limited partners and no operating track record
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Duly notarised partnership agreement (contrat de société), RCSL registration excerpt, RBE beneficial ownership extract, passport and proof of residence of each partner, source-of-wealth statement, business profile, and an anti-money laundering legal opinion from a Luxembourg-qualified attorney.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Fiscal transparency of the SCSp causing uncertainty over economic ownership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal opinion confirming the pass-through tax classification of the SCSp, a full list of partners with percentage interests and capital accounts, the commercial purpose and intended flow of funds through the partnership, and a partnership agreement containing clear limitations on liability and transfer rights.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: IoT hardware retail merchant with high-volume low-value e-commerce sales and no physical inventory in Luxembourg
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: E-commerce platform agreements with Shopify and Stripe, certified or audited financial statements, transaction history, logistics and shipping records, product catalogue and after-sales policy, invoice sample, returns report, and proof of commercial substance in Luxembourg such as sublease agreement and local compliance advisor engagement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border supplier payments to non-EU jurisdictions such as Hong Kong or mainland China
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original purchase invoices, purchase orders, customs declarations, Incoterms, supplier KYC profile, proof of goods consignment, transport and warehousing documentation, and a treasury policy identifying when the bank will use documentary letters of credit rather than open account SWIFT transfers.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For EU partners, capital contributions should be routed via SEPA Credit Transfer using ISO 20022 XML with a purpose code identifying a capital contribution and referencing the SCSp IBAN and partnership name. For non-EU investors, use SWIFT MT103 with clear field 70 beneficiary information stating 'Capital contribution to LU_SCSp' together with the partner's KYC reference and the BCL/ECB balance-of-payments statistical purpose category 'Direct investment – Equity capital'. The receiving bank will verify the transfer against the signed partnership agreement, the capital contribution statement, and the RBE beneficial ownership filing. Enhanced due diligence is triggered for transfers above EUR 100,000 and for any SDN, FATF, or EU-sanctioned jurisdiction check.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier settlements should be executed through SWIFT MT103 for USD, CNY, and other non-EUR currencies, or via SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR payments inside the EEA. For high-value IoT inventory purchases, an irrevocable documentary commercial letter of credit can be issued under UCP600 using SWIFT MT700. E-commerce platform funds collected by Stripe and Shopify Payments should be swept daily or weekly into the Luxembourg operational treasury account. All outbound wires must carry correct purpose codes, underlying invoices, customs references, and be screened against EU financial sanctions and Luxembourg export-control lists.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla over-the-counter FX forwards with value dates matching expected EUR/USD receipts and payable due dates
FX swaps and rollovers used for short-term liquidity management of working capital accounts
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for hedging long-term commercial financing exposure
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on restricted or non-fully convertible currencies such as offshore CNY where physical delivery is not possible
Exchange-traded FX futures cleared through regulated EU venues when required to complement OTC limits

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of RCS registration data (confirmation annuelle des données du RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually during the month of the anniversary of the entity's RCS registration (e.g., an entity registered in March must confirm during March of each year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal overdue notice from LBR; court-imposed fine on the general partner (up to EUR 5,000); repeated non-confirmation exposes the SCSp to compulsory dissolution and administrative strike-off from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owners (confirmation annuelle des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March of each calendar year; any change in beneficial ownership must be filed within one month of the triggering transaction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to EUR 10,000 for the SCSp and its general partner under the Law of 13 January 2019; continued default may trigger judicial enforcement, restrictions on distributions, and public registry penalty notices.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of annual statutory accounts (comptes annuels) with the court registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / RCS (greffe du tribunal de commerce)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven months of the financial year-end (31 July for a 31 December year-end); abridged accounts permitted for micro and small SCSp entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: RCS formal notice and court-imposed fine (generally EUR 100-EUR 5,000); the commercial court may order the general partner to file under penalty payment; persistent failure leads to strike-off and compulsory liquidation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent statutory audit (révision légale) is mandatory if the SCSp exceeds two of the three thresholds for two consecutive financial years: total balance sheet above EUR 4.4 million, net turnover above EUR 8.8 million (exclusive of VAT), or average headcount above 50 employees. Audit is also compulsory when any general partner is a Luxembourg public-interest entity or when required by the RAIF/SIF regime or by contractual lender covenants.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the amended Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies and the Law of 19 December 2002 on the accounting obligations of undertakings; IFRS as adopted by the EU may be used voluntarily for individual financial statements and is mandatory for consolidated accounts if the group opts for IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Law of 13 January 2019, the SCSp must identify all ultimate beneficial owners, record their shareholding/control percentages in the RBE file, and confirm the accuracy of that information annually by 31 March on the LBR portal. Any transfer of partnership interests or change in control must be declared to the RBE within one month; the general partner is personally responsible for submitting complete and accurate beneficial-ownership data.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (register of partners / associés)
Register of Directors (register of the general partner and management resolutions)
Minute Book (procès-verbaux of partner and management meetings)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 900 - USD 2,200 per year for a Luxembourg registered office, domiciliation agent and compliance-calendar monitoring service
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,500 - USD 11,500 for a first-time certified audit of a retail SCSp under Luxembourg GAAP, assuming small-to-medium size and abridged accounts

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% at SCSp level (fiscally transparent partnership); corporate partners subject to combined CIT of 24.94% in Luxembourg City (17% CIT + 5.25% municipal business tax + 7% solidarity surcharge) on their distributive share of profits
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday at SCSp level; participation exemption for qualifying shareholdings (>=10% holding and other conditions) exempts 100% of dividends and capital gains for corporate partners; IP box regime provides 80% exemption on qualifying IP income (effective ~5.1%); 30% notional deduction for equity financing may apply; tax transparency prevents entity-level tax leakage on distributions
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (Luxembourg LIR Art. 114 allows indefinite carryforward; limited anti-abuse where a >50% change in ownership is accompanied by a change in activity)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1002 (Declaration for fiscally transparent partnerships / sociétés de personnes) filed electronically via MyGuichet.lu (https://myguichet.lu) or through accredited accountant/auditor e-filing channels; economic operators may also use the Luxembourg direct tax portal ('eTax.lu') for related individual/corporate returns.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (calendar fiscal year or statutory accounting year; strictly annual with no interim CIT return obligation for the SCSp itself, though quarterly advance payments are due on behalf of partners' taxable income where applicable)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Deadline is 31 May of the year following the fiscal year-end for fiscal-transparent partnership returns; e-filing may automatically defer to 30 June; upon agent justification, the tax office may grant an extension to 31 December (subject to late interest if any balance remains unpaid).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name, legal form (SCSp), registered office, RCS Luxembourg registration number, national tax number (numéro d'identification fiscale), and contact details of the authorised representative.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident SCSp partners must provide their foreign tax ID, country of tax residence, permanent establishment neutrality confirmation, and CRS/FATCA self-certification (CRS form).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening and closing dates of the financial year (must coincide with balance sheet period).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the SCSp has a short first period, state the shorter period; ensure start date corresponds to RCS incorporation date unless a business combination recharacterizes it.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total net commercial profit or loss before partnership profit allocations, adjusted for tax amortisation, provisions, and disallowed expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where a non-resident partner is tax-transparent in its own jurisdiction, the Luxembourg result remains as computed under Luxembourg rules; the partner may attach its own tax analysis in an appendix.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: For each partner: full name/company name, address, tax residence, economic ownership percentage, profit-sharing percentage, and capital account movements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must state their Luxembourg permanent establishment (PE) status; if no PE, confirm that no Luxembourg source tax is due on such allocable share (no dividend WHT on SCSp distributions).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 (Foreign Tax Credits and Withholding Tax Recoveries)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of any foreign source income and withholding taxes paid that are eligible for credit or deduction at partner level.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners can claim the credit on their domestic return; Luxembourg does not issue a credit certificate to the SCSp, so partners should retain the Box 3 paper trail.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial statements, statutory auditor's report (if any), tax calculations of amortisations, capital gains, and evidence of arm's-length transfer pricing where cross-border related-party transactions exist.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where the SCSp engages in cross-border stock/royalty/intragroup transactions, non-resident partners should file a cooperative TP documentation set even below statutory thresholds to avoid automatic adjustments.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form 1002 triggers an administrative penalty up to EUR 1,500; late payment of partners' resulting tax liabilities attracts monthly interest of 0.8% (rationale: Art. 155 LIR); if the partnership deliberately under-declares or files late, a fine up to 10% of the concealed tax base may be imposed on partners jointly and severally.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory Luxembourg withholding tax on dividends paid by a real-estate rich Luxembourg corporation, but SCSp is fiscally transparent: distributions to partners are not subject to Luxembourg dividend WHT and are not treated as dividends; subsequent profit distributions by a corporate partner may be subject to Luxembourg WHT at 15% when paid to individual non-resident shareholders (reduced to 5% under DTA for qualifying corporate shareholders).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident partner seeking relief from Luxembourg dividend WHT on indirectly earned corporate profits must: (a) obtain a Luxembourg tax residence certificate (TRC) and a Form 5011 from its own tax authorities; (b) file a refund/relief claim with the Luxembourg Inland Revenue (Administration des contributions directes, taxpayer service) on form 23 (for dividends) within the statutory limitation period (generally two (2) years from the expiry of the calendar year in which the income was collected); (c) provide the SCSp's annual certificate of profit allocation (Box 5 above) and the underlying corporation's dividend coupon; (d) if DTA relief is claimed on favourable terms, submit the treaty-specific form (e.g. IRS Form 8833 for US partners, UK Form 62 for UK partners, Germany AA-Schengen proof) together with the partner's Luxembourg Form 1002 attribution statement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT rates: Luxembourg does not impose withholding tax on royalty payments (0% statutory rate); interest on non-securitised commercial loans and bank debt is generally not subject to Luxembourg WHT (0%); however, a 15% WHT applies to interest paid on 'profit participating loan certificates' (genussrechte) where the interest is tied to profits and on interest paid by a Luxembourg entity to a resident of a tax haven (equalisation tax of 10% under Article 168 LIR). Under current DTAs, Luxembourg treaty rates typically reduce applicable thresholds to 0-10% on royalties, 0-10% on interest, and 5-15% on dividends, with zero WHT commonly for EU parent companies holding 10% or more.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 50 million group consolidated revenue triggers the mandatory preparation of a Master File and a Luxembourg Local File; an additional activity threshold requires Local File preparation where the Luxembourg entity's related-party cross-border transactions exceed EUR 1 million for goods/services royalties (or EUR 250,000 for intragroup financing transactions). Below these thresholds, a 'light' TP file (functional analysis, pricing evidence, comparability analysis) must be available upon request to justify arm's-length behaviour; the SCSp's IoT retail operations normally have no regulatory licence, so the TP risk is limited to payments for intragroup procurement, e-commerce platform fees, IP licensing, and group management charges.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg has no dedicated standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) equivalent to the Cayman or UAE codes, but fiscally transparent SCSp must prove real economic presence in Luxembourg to preserve treaty access and to avoid being recharacterised as a domestic taxable company under General Anti-Abuse Rule (GAAR). The tax administration applies the OECD BEPS substance indicators: local management, full-time employees, active decision-making in Luxembourg, adequate IT infrastructure, and a physical office. A pure letterbox SCSp engaged in IoT retail with no personnel or operational substance will be denied DTA benefits, and profits may be retroactively reallocated to the controlling partner's jurisdiction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion – deliberate concealment of income or profits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Scientifically or recklessly omitting IoT hardware sales revenue, overstating Shopify/Stripe transaction deductions, or misallocating SCSp income to a non-resident partner without fiscal transparency documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty up to 10% of the recalculated taxable base, increased to 50% in cases of fraud; criminal fine up to EUR 25,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years; plus monthly late interest (0.8%) accruing from the due date.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and SCSp general partners may be jointly and severally liable for the amount of unpaid corporate tax and interest where the tax loss is attributable to their wilful misconduct; courts may impose travel bans, asset freezes, and a prohibition on exercising management functions in Luxembourg for up to 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / letterbox SCSp (no economic substance)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining an SCSp entity with no local office, no staff, no local management, and no business documentation, while routing IoT e-commerce revenues and Intragroup funds through Luxembourg purely to access tax-treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation as a fully taxable Luxembourg corporation; denial of the SCSp's pass-through treatment; reassessment of corporate tax at 24.94% plus penalties up to 10% of previously avoided tax; potential 10% equalisation tax on payments to non-cooperative tax havens; under the EU ATAD, an exit tax may also be triggered.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partners are personally liable for the SCSp's tax deficiencies up to the full amount of unpaid tax and penalties; courts can order civil restitution of evaded taxes plus interest, and impose director disqualification orders, asset seizures and travel bans pending recovery.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the SCSp as a conduit to process IoT retail payment card transactions without performing AML customer due diligence, beneficial-ownership disclosure, and e-money transaction monitoring, or allowing the unlicensed routing of funds through Stripe/Shopify without Luxembourg AML registration under CSSF Regulation 12-02.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CSSF administrative fine up to EUR 5 million or 10% of annual turnover for legal persons; imprisonment of up to 5 years for individuals; mandatory liquidation notifications; revocation of banking/payment licences (if any) and public disclosure of sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and partners face personal criminal liability, disqualification from board positions, and direct civil restitution of funds laundered through the SCSp; travel bans and preventive non-conviction based confiscation orders may be issued by Luxembourg courts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Invoicing IoT hardware procurement or cross-border royalty/services without an arm's-length pricing benchmark; setting purchase prices materially above market so the Luxembourg SCSp's taxable profit is artificially shifted to a low-tax jurisdiction within the same group.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax corrections (upward adjustment of taxable income) plus a 10% non-deductible penalty on the adjusted amount if TP documentation was absent; late interest at 0.8%/month; in serious cases, secondary adjustment and equalization tax may apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign the return and deliberately approve the false TP policy are personally jointly liable for the adjustment and penalties; criminal sanctions for qualified negligence can include imprisonment up to 2 years, travel bans, and a prohibition on managing a commercial entity in the EEA.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to File Tax Return / Persistent Non-Compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Systematically disregarding the annual Form 1002 filing obligation, failing to declare the SCSp's profit allocation to partners, or ignoring a Luxembourg tax office preliminary assessment within the 30-day responding period.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Lump-sum penalty up to EUR 1,200 per missed return plus 10% of the estimated unpaid tax; if non-filing is deemed fraudulent, the penalty increases to 50% of assessed tax, and criminal fines up to EUR 12,500 can be ordered; the tax office may issue an estimated assessment (taxation d'office) that treats the SCSp as taxable at 24.94%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the general partner are jointly and severally liable for all taxes assessed on the d'office basis, including penalties and monthly interest; courts may issue a payment order attaching personal bank accounts, and a travel ban limiting departure from Luxembourg until sufficient assets are confiscated.
